method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Intravenous route only.** UFH is compatible with 5% dextrose and 0.9% sodium chloride.
claims.source_text: At RCH we only administer UFH by intravenous route. This guideline applies to the intravenous route only. UFH is compatible with 5% Dextrose and 0.9% NaCl
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every order must state:** total units in the syringe (no abbreviation for units), units/kg/hour, mL/hour, and an individualised target APTT range. If any is missing, the order must be recharted.
claims.source_text: Intravenous orders for UFH must state ALL of the following: Total Dose (in units) of UFH in a prepared syringe. No abbreviation for units will be accepted Dose (in units) to be infused per kilogram per hour (eg 20 units/kg/hour) Volume (mL) to be infused per hour. Individualised Target APTT range … If any of these details are missing, the prescribing doctor needs to rechart the order
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Baseline FBE, APTT, INR, creatinine and renal function.** Discuss any low platelet count or abnormal APTT or INR with a haematologist first.
claims.source_text: Obtain baseline FBE, APTT, INR, Creatinine and renal function. … Any patient with a low platelet count or an abnormal APTT or INR should be discussed with a Haematologist prior to starting UFH.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Concentrations by weight:** 1000 units in 50 mL under 10 kg · 5000 units in 50 mL for 10–40 kg · 10,000 units in 50 mL over 40 kg. Fluid-restricted patients may need stronger solutions — extra vigilance and a Haematology consult.
claims.source_text: 1000 units in 50 mL (for patients <10 kg) 5000 units in 50 mL (for patients >10 kg and <40 kg) 10,000 units in 50 mL (for patients >40 kg) … Patients that are fluid restricted may require more concentrated UFH solutions than that recommended based on weight. If this is necessary, increased vigilance is required and a Clinical Haematology consult is highly recommended.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Starting maintenance rate:** under 1 year 25 units/kg/hour · over 1 year 20 units/kg/hour · column headed '16 years' 18 units/kg/hr. **Renal failure needs modified doses** — discuss with Clinical Haematology.
claims.source_text: Patients with renal failure will require modified doses and should be discussed with Clinical Haematology. … <1 year >1 year 16 years Maintenance 25 units/kg/hour 20 units/kg/hour 18 units/kg/hr
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cap: under 83 kg, the maximum starting rate is 1500 units/hr.** **No bolus on commencement** unless Clinical Haematology specifically requests it.
claims.source_text: NB For patients weighing <83 kg, max commencement rate = 1500 units/hr … Bolus doses of UFH on commencement of therapy are NOT recommended unless specifically requested by the Clinical Haematology team
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rate (mL/hour) = weight × dose (units/kg/hr) ÷ concentration (units/mL).** Use a **dedicated line**; do not stop or interrupt it for other medication.
claims.source_text: Patient Weight x Dose Required (units/kg/hr) / Heparin concentration (units/mL) = mLs/hour to be infused … Patients should have a dedicated line for UFH infusions. The infusion should not be stopped or interrupted for other medication.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First APTT 6 hours after starting** (to catch supra-therapeutic levels; a dose change may not be needed). Usually no need to wake patients overnight. **Most patients then need one APTT every 24 hours.**
claims.source_text: Obtain venous blood sample for an APTT assay 6 hours post UFH commencement, or as directed by the Clinical Haematology department. In most instances, it is not necessary to wake patients overnight for UFH monitoring tests. This checking of the APTT is to ensure patients are not supra-therapeutic. A UFH dose change may not be required. … For most patients one APTT assay every 24 hours is sufficient.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Where APTT may be inaccurate, anti-Xa may be used:** 0.35–0.7 units/mL is therapeutic in adult studies; consult Clinical Haematology.
claims.source_text: In some clinical scenarios, the APTT may not be accurate, and an anti-Xa assay may be used. Within adult based studies, an anti-Xa assay of 0.35-0.7 units/mL equates to a therapeutic UFH dose. Consultation with the Clinical Haematology unit is recommended in such scenarios.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nomogram, low APTT:** under 50 s — increase 20%, repeat in 4 hours (a bolus may be appropriate; consult Haematology) · 50–59 s — increase 10%, repeat in 6 hours · **60–85 s — no change**, repeat in 24 hours.
claims.source_text: APTT(seconds) BOLUS (units/kg) Hold(minutes) Rate change (units/hr) Repeat APTT … <50 * 0 Increase 20% 4 hours 50-59 0 0 Increase 10% 6 hours 60-85 0 0 No change 24 hours … *Bolus may be appropriate depending on clinical situation and perceived bleeding risk. Consult the Clinical Haematology department.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nomogram, high APTT:** 86–95 s — reduce 10% · 96–120 s — hold 30 minutes, reduce 10% · **over 120 s — hold 60 minutes, reduce 15%**; repeat APTT in 6 hours for each. Changes are a percentage of the units/kg/hour rate.
claims.source_text: APTT(seconds) BOLUS (units/kg) Hold(minutes) Rate change (units/hr) Repeat APTT … 86-95 0 0 Reduce 10% 6 hours 96-120 0 30 Reduce 10% 6 hours >120 0 60 Reduce 15% 6 hours … The rate changes suggested in the table above are to be calculated as a percentage of the total infusion, that is, in units/kg/hour.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not turn off the infusion to take an APTT or anti-Xa**, and **do not sample from the heparin line or limb**; if unavoidable, discard at least 5 mL first. Fill coagulation tubes exactly to the mark.
claims.source_text: Do NOT turn off UFH infusion prior to collecting an APTT or anti-Xa assay. … APTT blood samples should NOT be drawn from the same line (or limb) as the UFH infusion. If this cannot be avoided, a minimum discard volume of 5 mL should be collected prior to collecting the APTT or Anti-Xa sample. … Coagulation tubes must be filled exactly to the specified mark to avoid erroneous results.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Twice-weekly FBE (platelets) and renal function.** An abrupt platelet fall (e.g. 50%) → consult Clinical Haematology. After two failed venous APTT attempts, contact Haematology before trying again.
claims.source_text: Twice weekly FBEs, (platelet count) and renal function are required. If there is an abrupt decrease in platelet count, (eg 50%) consult the Clinical Haematology department. … If two unsuccessful attempts to obtain a venous APTT have occurred, contact the Clinical Haematology department before further attempts are made.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No lumbar punctures on UFH.** Avoid IM injections, arterial stabs, aspirin and other antiplatelet drugs. Withhold UFH before procedures — timing with Haematology.
claims.source_text: Avoid IM injections and arterial stabs during anticoagulant therapy. … Lumbar punctures should not be performed while patients are on UFH therapy. Avoid aspirin and other anti-platelet medications during UFH therapy. UFH should be withheld prior to procedures. … Clinical Haematology consultation is recommended in determining the timing of UFH cessation around procedures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bleeding is the major adverse event: if it occurs, cease the UFH infusion and seek urgent Clinical Haematology consult.** Screening for HIT requires Haematology consultation.
claims.source_text: The major adverse event potentially related to UFH infusion is bleeding. … If a patient on UFH develops bleeding, cease UFH infusion and seek urgent Clinical Haematology consult. … Screening for the possibility of HIT requires Clinical Haematology consultation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stopping the infusion usually suffices; for an immediate effect consider protamine sulfate.** Outside cardiac surgery and ICU, protamine needs Clinical Haematology approval — **but do not let this delay it in bleeding.**
claims.source_text: If anticoagulation with UFH needs to be discontinued for clinical reasons, termination of the UFH infusion will usually suffice. If an immediate effect is required, consider administering protamine sulfate. … Outside of cardiac surgery and ICU, Clinical Haematology approval is required for the use of protamine – do not allow this to lead to delayed administration in the case of bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Protamine per 100 units of UFH received in the previous 2 hours**, by time since last UFH: under 30 min 1 mg · 30–60 min 0.5–0.75 mg · 60–120 min 0.375–0.5 mg · over 120 min 0.25–0.375 mg.
claims.source_text: The dose of protamine sulfate is based on the amount of UFH received in the previous 2 hours as follows: … Time since Last UFH Dose Protamine Dose (mg) per 100units UFH received <30 min 1 mg 30-60 min 0.5-0.75 mg 60-120 min 0.375-0.5 mg >120 min 0.25-0.375 mg
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Maximum protamine 50 mg** (except after cardiopulmonary bypass), usually as 10 mg/mL, **no faster than 5 mg/minute — too fast can cause cardiovascular collapse.** Check PT and APTT 15 min after.
claims.source_text: The maximum dose of protamine sulfate, regardless of the amount of UFH received is 50 mg except for reversal of UFH following cardiopulmonary bypass. Protamine sulfate is usually administered in a concentration of 10 mg/mL at a rate not to exceed 5 mg/minute. If administered too quickly, protamine sulfate may cause cardiovascular collapse. … Obtain blood for PT and APTT 15 min after the administration of protamine sulfate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hypersensitivity risk:** fish allergy, previous protamine-containing insulin or previous protamine.
claims.source_text: Patients with known hypersensitivity reactions to fish, and those who have received protamine- containing insulin or previous protamine therapy may be at risk of hypersensitivity reactions to protamine sulfate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Requires Clinical Haematology involvement.** **Indications:** massive PE · PE not responding to heparin · arterial occlusion threatening organ or limb · acute extensive DVT threatening organ or limb.
claims.source_text: Administration of systemic lytic therapy within the RCH requires involvement of the Clinical Haematology department. … Massive pulmonary embolism Pulmonary embolism not responding to heparin Arterial occlusions threatening organ or limb viability Potential for acute, extensive DVT threatening organ or limb viability.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Contraindications:** active bleeding · significant risk of serious local bleeding · general surgery within 10 days · neurosurgery within 3 weeks · AV malformations · recent significant trauma.
claims.source_text: Contraindications Active bleeding Significant potential for serious local bleeding General surgery within the previous 10 days Neurosurgery within the previous 3 weeks AV malformations Recent significant trauma.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before lysis:** platelet count must be over 100; give FFP 20 mL/kg if clinically indicated; consider vitamin K. **Run heparin 10 units/kg/hour throughout lysis**, ideally starting 6 hours before.
claims.source_text: Platelet count must be >100. … Administer FFP infusion 20ml/kg if clinically indicated. Consider administering Vitamin K if the patient could be deficient. … Establish heparin infusion of 10 units/kg/hour to be administered continuously throughout lytic infusion … If possible heparin should be administered for 6 hours prior to lysis as this may reduce the likelihood of thrombus progression.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **tPA is the preferred agent: 0.5 mg/kg/hour over 6 hours, no loading dose.** Streptokinase (never after previous streptokinase exposure; premedicate with paracetamol and/or promethazine): 2000 units/kg over 10 minutes, then 1000 units/kg/hour over 6 hours, max loading 250,000 units.
claims.source_text: tPA is the preferred lytic agent for use in children … TPA No* 0.5 mg/kg/hour over 6 hours. n/a Streptokinase 2000 units/kg over 10 minutes 1000 units/kg/hour over 6 hours 250,000 units … DO NOT use Streptokinase if the patient has previously been exposed to streptokinase. Premedicate with paracetamol and/or promethazine due to potential for allergic reactions.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Monitor:** pulse and BP hourly; puncture sites hourly and for 4 hours after; fibrinogen at 3 hours and at completion. **Stop lysis at 6 hours, then increase heparin to 20 units/kg/hour (no bolus)** and arrange Haematology review.
claims.source_text: Throughout infusion monitor: - pulse & BP hourly Inspect all puncture sites hourly during infusion and for 4 hours post infusion Check Fibrinogen 3 hours into infusion and at completion … Cease lytic therapy at 6 hours. Increase heparin to 20 units/kg/hour (no bolus). Arrange Clinical Haematology review to determine response or need for further lysis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any bleeding or bruising: cease tPA and heparin and seek urgent Haematology review.** Local pressure usually suffices for wound or puncture-site oozing; cryoprecipitate, antifibrinolytics and blood products may be needed for major bleeding. **No IM injections; avoid warfarin and antiplatelet agents.**
claims.source_text: If any signs of bleeding and/or bruising occur– cease tPA and Heparin infusions and seek urgent Clinical Haematology consult … Treatment with local pressure is usually sufficient management of bleeding from wound or puncture sites. Cryoprecipitate, antifibrinolytics and blood products may be indicated for the management of major bleeding. … No IM injections during lytic therapy Minimize patient handling during infusion Avoid concurrent use of warfarin and antiplatelet agents
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Anticoagulation therapy' (undated page), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Anticoagulation_therapy/, retrieved 2026-09-23
